name: The Branching Maze
tagline: Read the walls, recover from dead ends, and find the exit.
narrative: This is a maze, not a corridor with decorative walls. The exit lies beyond several junctions, and plausible-looking routes end abruptly. A robot that blindly repeats a turn will spend its run trapped in a branch. Build a small set of rules that responds to the walls it can sense and keeps making progress through the maze.
objective: Reach the exit of the 11×11 Branching Maze, then hold on the goal for 3 ticks.
learningObjective: Applying ordered rules and wall observations to navigate a branching layout with genuine dead ends.
intelligenceExplanation: The robot has the navigation primitives but no strategy. It needs a first arrival rule, a rule for a blocked path, and a safe fallback for open space. The order matters: safety and arrival decisions must appear before ordinary movement. You may compose a reusable movement brick if it helps keep the rule set clear.
hint: Start with WHEN atGoal → DO hold. Then decide what should happen when wallAhead is true before adding your forward-movement fallback. Test at each junction; a rule that works in a corridor may loop in a dead end.
hints: Protect the goal first: an atGoal / hold rule at the top stops the robot from walking away.
A blocked route must be handled before the generic movement rule; use wallAhead and a pivot.
Try a consistent wall-following policy: take an open side when possible, otherwise go forward, otherwise turn away from the wall. Keep those rules in that order.
brief: Use a consistent ordered navigation policy to escape the branching maze.
context: Several plausible routes terminate in dead ends, so corridor-only rules are not enough.

steps.label: Handle side openings, clear paths, and blocked routes
